title: Royal toll exemption
setup: Trump tried to end New York’s congestion toll and posted “Long Live the King.” A judge blocked the attempt. At a carpool picnic, a visiting New York courier shows his bill. Hosts invite supplies for recording drivers’ accounts, or some food to share. His bill accepts money, not royal proclamations.

choices.label: Donate supplies to record drivers’ accounts
choices.outcome: You donate supplies and preserve the accounts. The courier attaches the presidential post to his toll bill. They disagree about who is running the kingdom.

choices.label: Share some food; hear the courier’s story
choices.outcome: You share some food and hear his story. “I tried saying Long Live the King at the toll bill,” he says. “Turns out it wanted Long Live My Debit Card.”

choices.label: Compare and save the toll maps
choices.outcome: You save the old and current toll maps and make sense of the ruling. The courier puts away his toy crown. The border of Manhattan remains unmoved by headwear.
